text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King emphasises the need to continue the peace process, Crown Prince reviews with Russian Foreign Minister Primakov latest Middle East developments.
- Crown Prince Hassan returns back to the country, emphasises the "importance of integration and partnership for peace and development."
- Kabariti discusses with Omani and Tunisian officials coordinating Arab stances in the Cairo economic summit.
- State-sector doctors call for extraordinary meeting to discuss pay dispute with the government.

- King Hussein, in a meeting with the Russian foreign minister, emphasises the importance of resumption of the peace process on all tracks; Crown Prince Hassan discusses with Primakov means of activating the Middle East peace process multilateral talks.
- Suicide of a young couple in tragic love affair in the city of Jerash.
- Palestinian delegation arrives on Sunday to start official talks with the government.
- Three projects for special trade zones, peace airport and a communications network to be presented to the Cairo economic summit, all approved by the Jordan Rift Valley steering committee.
- Consensus on al-Aswaq's initiative for holding a national conference on sports.
- Arrest of a car theft gang that stole the contents of 120 cars in southern Amman area.
- Iran nominates a new ambassador to Jordan.
- Amman Municipality studies draft law that will allow 15 storey buildings in the Amman area, and the setting up of projects and investment complexes are the main highlights of the proposed law.
- The cabinet appoints the official delegation to the Cairo economic summit, headed by Minister of Trade and Industry, Ali Abu al-Ragheb.
